Definition: from G3664; to assimilate, i.e. compare; passively, to become similar:--be (make) like, (in the) liken(-ess), resemble.
BiblicalUsage: When Scripture says homoióō, it means be (make) like, (in the) liken, resemble. The word appears 15 times, and in Matthew, Mark, Luke, and Acts it carries that same straightforward meaning. Nothing hidden sits behind it; the sense is the one you would expect from the word itself.
TheologicalSignificance: homoióō matters to me because we are made in God’s likeness, and Christ restores what sin broke. My position is simple: I take God at His word here, and I build on that.
RelatedEvents: The Parable of the Mustard Seed; The Children in the Marketplace; Paul Stoned at Lystra
